paragraphs: Coroners carry statutory coordination of death investigations, but how the position is created, whether it must be held by a physician, and whether it can order an autopsy or issue documents all vary by jurisdiction; the core is to turn the scene, the body, identity, medical history and examination materials into a traceable conclusion.
Suitable for a first try: able to face death, trauma materials and family emotions while staying accurate and respectful; willing to repeatedly verify identity, timelines and the chain of evidence.
Choose with caution: not suited to people who pursue quick conclusions or avoid sensitive communication.

Low-risk verification: complete the fictional exercise on this page and only judge whether you are willing to do verification, recording and escalation; do not touch bodies or real cases, do not infer cause or manner of death, and do not give conclusions to families or law enforcement.

U.S. O*NET 13-1041.06 describes directing investigations of accidental, violent or undetermined deaths. Outputs include death certificates and determinations of cause and manner of death, investigation reports, transfer of evidence and the body, family notification and judicial cooperation; the specific authority of the position depends on the jurisdiction.

Real inputs include reports and scene observations, body and identity information, medical history, witness statements, photographs, the chain of physical evidence, toxicology or pathology results and law enforcement records.

Editorial process summary: verify jurisdiction and identity, record the scene and body, conduct interviews and take medical history, preserve and transfer physical evidence, examine or arrange autopsy and pathology and toxicology testing, and produce the reports and documents one is authorized to sign. O*NET also lists forensic examination/autopsy and directing autopsies as tasks, so it cannot be summarized as all coroners only organizing paperwork; the executing parties and authorization must be checked separately.

The key judgment is to distinguish observation, testimony and professional inference, and to decide which matters require the involvement of forensic physicians, pathology, toxicology, law enforcement or the courts.
Tools include case management and death registration systems, photography and measurement tools, and evidence packaging and transfer records; modern data systems are not equal to generative AI.
Collaboration partners include forensic physicians or pathologists, death investigators, law enforcement, public health, medical institutions, funeral service providers and the decedent's family.

Quality requires that identity, timelines, evidence numbers, transfers, examinations and corrections be traceable. Of the current 57 O*NET context items: 70% of respondents are exposed to disease and infection daily, 50% face strict deadlines daily, 60% usually work more than 40 hours per week and 55% work irregular hours; these are U.S. respondent distributions, not Chinese proportions or guarantees about personal scheduling.

A coroner may determine cause and manner of death under law and bear signing and court testimony responsibility; medical procedures, performance of autopsies, jurisdiction and signing authority are each checked against current law. O*NET 13-1041.06 is Job Zone 3／SVP 6 to less than 7; the position level description is not a legal qualification. Among education responses, 35% bachelor's degree, 15% associate's or two-year degree and 15% post-baccalaureate certificate, with the remaining proportions not shown and not filled in. The CDC 2024 summary states that coroner qualifications and how the position is filled differ by state, and the older state profiles were published in 2015; current application and medical requirements must be checked in the target jurisdiction.
Coroner: whether the position is filled by election or appointment, what professional background is required and which duties may be performed all depend first on state and local systems.
Medical examiner: usually a physician-led medicolegal death investigation system; the coroner entry path cannot be applied directly to this direction.
Medicolegal death investigator: leans more toward the scene and records and identity and evidence chain coordination, and authorization is still decided by the specific agency and jurisdiction.
Forensic science technicians: mainly collect, preserve or analyze criminal and physical evidence materials, and the work object and laboratory deliverables differ from statutory death rulings.

The public health death data direction focuses on death certificate quality and statistics; it differs from legal authority in individual cases, and before moving across you must separate case work, laboratory work and data work.
Editorial reasoning: tools can organize case file fields, timelines and missing items in an approved, de-identified environment; this is not evidence of agency adoption.

Editorial reasoning: they can generate record completeness checklists or draft documents, but must not determine identity, jurisdiction, cause of death, manner of death or evidence authenticity. AI Impact Score 33% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((50+25+25)/3+0.5)=33; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.
Failure modes include fabricating case facts, merging people with the same name, reversing timelines, mismatching evidence numbers, or writing a probability as a statutory conclusion.

Before adoption, jurisdiction rules, criminal justice and health data permissions, the chain of evidence, audit logs, procurement and validation requirements must be met; this page has no deployment rate evidence.
Human control means going back item by item to scene records, identity materials, transfer forms and examination reports, with review and signature by those holding the corresponding authority.
This page takes a conservative usage boundary: the model is not allowed to decide jurisdiction, order an autopsy, sign a death certificate, notify families of conclusions or alter evidence records.

Remaining human responsibilities include scene judgment, body examination or coordination, family communication, cross-agency evidence gathering, statutory determinations and court testimony responsibility.
Existing sources do not show that generative AI causes a net increase or decrease in the number of coroner positions.

Articles 2 and 4—7 of the Ministry of Justice's Provisions on the Classification of Practice for Forensic Judicial Appraisal cover forensic appraisal for specialized litigation issues, forensic pathology, postmortem examination and determination of manner of death; they describe the relevant business, do not establish a position or wage in one-to-one correspondence with the U.S. coroner, and do not provide the complete entry conditions for the target units on this page. The precise Chinese counterpart identity and the national occupational wage are still missing. If a real employer's main business is scientific research and technical services, reference may be made to NBS2025 non-private 182,064／private 83,560 yuan pretax annual average; if the main business is health and social work, reference may be made to 146,266／75,631 yuan; for public administration, social security and social organizations only the non-private figure of 119,465 yuan is available. This page does not confirm the specific unit classification and does not treat these industry-wide all-position averages as the median or starting salary of forensic physicians or coroners, nor does it convert them into personal monthly income or take-home pay.

The NBS unit average wage divides the total wage bill by the average number of employed persons and includes bonuses, allowances and overtime pay; the 2025 survey covers urban legal entities with 5 or more people and does not cover self-employed and freelance workers. Industry averages cannot be used to infer an occupation's wage distribution, an entry-level starting wage or personal net income.
A real comparison should record the city, employer, position tasks, contract, shifts, benefits, qualifications and the date of the information.

Single-occupation pay in China remains an evidence gap; the industry background can bound the comparison, is not zero income, and is not replaced with U.S. parent-occupation pay. AI case file assistance is likewise editorial reasoning, with no sample of Chinese agency adoption or pay effects.
U.S. parent occupation data, accessed 2026: compliance officers (13-1041, parent occupation proxy) had a 2025 median annual wage of $80,730.
U.S. parent occupation data, accessed 2026: compliance officers (13-1041, parent occupation proxy) had 2025 employment of 436,400 people.
U.S. parent occupation data, accessed 2026: compliance officers (13-1041, parent occupation proxy) had a 2025—2035 projected employment change of 3.8%.
U.S. parent occupation data, accessed 2026: compliance officers (13-1041, parent occupation proxy) had an average of 32,700 job openings per year over 2025—2035.

BLS Table 1.2 only provides the median annual wage for this parent occupation and does not provide an independent percentile or starting wage for coroners. The median is not a starting wage, employment is a stock, and annual average openings include replacement demand. OEWS covers pretax regular monetary wages for wage and salary jobs and excludes self-employed workers, direct household employees and unpaid family workers; it excludes benefits and overtime premiums and does not infer personal take-home pay.

Comparing real positions also requires checking location, employer, shifts, contract, benefits and qualifications; a parent occupation proxy especially cannot replace data for the target detailed occupation.
Able to face death, trauma materials and family emotions while staying accurate and respectful.
Willing to repeatedly verify identity, timelines and the chain of evidence.
Able to distinguish first-hand observation, other people's statements and professional inference.

Can you stay accurate under the irregular hours or long shifts that occur in actual positions? 55% of O*NET respondents report irregular hours and 60% work more than 40 hours per week, which does not mean every position involves night shifts.
Willing to collaborate with law enforcement, medical, forensic and public health parties.
Able to clearly mark what remains to be verified when information is incomplete, rather than making it up.

Editorial self-question: when information is insufficient, emotions run high or you are being rushed, can you slow the conclusion, explain what needs checking and communicate respectfully? This is used to observe training needs and cannot be used to judge suitability from a single performance or a personality label.
When comparing positions, check whether the role is elected or appointed, the medical qualifications, the scene tasks and the signing authority.

When state and county systems and position authority are inconsistent, the decedent's family, investigators and subsequent judicial proceedings may face being unable to accept a case or invalid records; the person handling it should first verify the jurisdiction and agency responsibilities and stop making substantive judgments if they cannot be confirmed.

An incomplete scene, identity or chain of evidence hinders the reconstruction of facts. NIJ guidelines require considering scene safety first, then recording the scene and physical evidence according to authority and preserving transfer information at each step; do not treat 'preserve the original state' as an instruction that allows ignoring rescue or continuing exposure to danger.

Writing preliminary observations as a final cause or manner of death misleads families, public records and judicial users; scene personnel should clearly mark them as provisional and retain the basis, and the final conclusion is formed by the qualified personnel and procedures specified locally.

When death certificate fields are missing or a generic template is applied, registration agencies and public health statistics may receive erroneous data; the person filling it in should check against the individual case materials and local rules, and refer doubts to the responsible person designated by the jurisdiction for confirmation.

Infection, contamination, weather and confined scenes can endanger those who respond; NIJ requires identifying safety risks and cooperating, and NET70% of O*NET respondents are exposed to disease and infection daily. Editorial suggestion: decide on entry, protection and exposure reporting according to the agency's risk assessment and authority; no complete suspension and recovery procedure for specific scenes or autopsies was obtained, so no general steps to follow are provided.

The first step is not signing up for a course, but confirming whether the target county or state uses a coroner or a medical examiner system, whether the position is filled by election or appointment, the minimum qualifications and whether a medical background is required; these can only be answered by that jurisdiction's official rules, and a generic certificate cannot be exchanged directly for the position.

This round did not obtain samples of recruitment or appointment announcements, so the content of announcements cannot be summarized or the real number of vacancies inferred; the editorial suggestion is to record the jurisdiction, nature of the position, term, pay and the date of the information source when comparing, and to distinguish among coroner, medical examiner, death investigator and forensic technician positions.

rows: Death investigation support and records position (supervised)
Assist with notification and response, on-scene records, decedent identity and body information, and evidence and transfer records under agency authorization.
Does not rule on cause or manner of death and does not sign death certificates; stop and escalate once outside authorization.
Able to keep records according to the NIJ2024 six-chapter framework; the guidelines are not a nationally uniform six-step process or a statutory entry requirement.
First confirm the target jurisdiction's official qualifications and recruitment process, then consider supervised support positions.
Coroner (elected or appointed)
Organize or carry out death investigations within the statutory jurisdiction, determine cause or manner of death under local law and sign the relevant documents.
Whether the holder must be a physician, whether autopsies can be ordered and whether there is a subordinate team are all decided by state and local rules.
Able to explain, in the wording of the jurisdiction's own text, how the position is filled, the scope of authority and the boundaries of responsibility.
Check that county's or state's current regulations and position description for coroner, rather than generic training advertisements.
Medical examiner (physician-led)
Medical examiners in the CDC summary are usually led by medical professionals; whether a specific position requires a physician and forensic pathology training is checked against current state law.
Medical or pathology training and statutory position conditions are checked separately, and coroner experience cannot automatically substitute for them.
Able to check that state's statutory requirements and appointment method for the medical examiner system.
Check the medical training path and the coroner path separately and do not apply one to the other.
Medicolegal death investigator (death investigator)
Responsible for scene response, records of the decedent and evidence, communication with families and law enforcement, and case file coordination.

The jurisdiction and agency decide actual authorization. NIJ2024 includes initial jurisdiction screening and recording of reasons, reviewed by the coroner／medical examiner; it cannot be said that an MDI makes no statutory judgments at all, nor can the guidelines confer authority to perform autopsies or sign documents.
Able to provide supervised samples of scene records, chain of evidence and case file coordination.
Check whether the target agency has separate qualification and training requirements for this position.
Forensic science technicians (adjacent)
Collect, preserve or analyze criminal and physical evidence materials and deliver laboratory results.
The work object and statutory death rulings differ, so the positions cannot be interchanged based on their names.
Able to explain the operational evidence of physical evidence handling and laboratory delivery.

BLS states that forensic science technicians usually have a bachelor's degree, with some positions requiring an associate's degree; handling cases independently may additionally require a competency examination or laboratory approval. This is separate from coroner qualifications.

Among education responses, 35% bachelor's degree, 15% associate's or two-year degree and 15% post-baccalaureate certificate, with the remaining proportions not shown and not filled in. The CDC 2024 summary states that coroner qualifications and how the position is filled differ by state, and the older state profiles were published in 2015; current application and medical requirements must be checked in the target jurisdiction.

Articles 2 and 4—7 of the Ministry of Justice's Provisions on the Classification of Practice for Forensic Judicial Appraisal cover forensic appraisal for specialized litigation issues, forensic pathology, postmortem examination and determination of manner of death; they describe the relevant business, do not establish a position or wage in one-to-one correspondence with the U.S. coroner, and do not provide the complete entry conditions for the target units on this page. The complete qualifications of the specific target units are still missing, and the business classification is not treated as a license condition.
Health and safety operating conditions

NIJ2024 emphasizes identifying physical, chemical and biological scene risks and collaborating; O*NET includes an infection exposure response. The editorial suggestion is to verify protection, exposure reporting and psychological support arrangements with the target agency; this round has no sample of uniform requirements across employers.
This page does not constitute safe operation, equipment use or clinical authorization; it must be checked against the agency's current safety procedures.
Observable professional ability evidence

Able to maintain precise, traceable records across decedent identity and the body, scene medical and investigation records, and death certificates and evidence; able to distinguish observation, statements and professional inference and to escalate proactively (from O*NET 13-1041.06 tasks and work context).
These are task and context observation points, not personality labels or hiring thresholds.
Common tools and system scope

Case file and death registration/reporting systems, photography and measurement tools, evidence packaging and transfer records, and submission processes with pathology and toxicology laboratories; data modernization emphasizes standard fields, permissions and exchange rather than replacing investigative judgment.
These tools can be used for task preparation; this round has no hiring sample proving their uniform weight, and proficiency is not equal to qualification or authorization.
Work sample one: arrival and scene record checklist
Deliverable: a fully fictional arrival record checklist, including notification and response, arrival time, scene and body observations, and numbering and transfer.
State the source of each item of information (scene observation, another person's statement or pending testing), and times and numbers must not contradict each other.
Work sample two: chain of evidence and record gap table
Deliverable: a one-page table listing the factual materials, transfers that have occurred, items still to be verified and the responsible parties.
Distinguish facts from inferences, mark gaps as 'to be verified' and do not make anything up.
Work sample three: escalation and boundary statement
Deliverable: a passage explaining which matters are outside your authority (jurisdiction, cause of death, manner of death, notifying families or signing documents) and to whom you should escalate.
Do not use real body images or personal medical information.
Work sample four: review note
Deliverable: a one-page note explaining which step took the most time, where errors are most likely and what you will supplement next, and noting that all materials used are fictional.

rows: Jurisdiction and qualification check
Able to clearly explain whether the target county or state uses a coroner or a medical examiner system, how the position is filled, the minimum qualifications and the source of authority.
Answer from the jurisdiction's official rules or position description, not from training advertisements.
Qualifications and authority follow the current rules of that jurisdiction; this page does not constitute a hiring or qualification conclusion.
Records and chain of evidence scenario
Use a fictional case to explain how to record arrival, identity and the body, numbering and transfer, and mark conflicts and items to be verified.
Distinguish observation, statements and inference, and clearly mark what needs verification when information is missing.
The scenario is designed by the recruiting agency, and this page does not infer specific assessment standards.
Communication and privacy boundaries
How to communicate with families, law enforcement and public health agencies when information is unconfirmed, and how to protect sensitive information.
Neither give conclusions prematurely nor disclose unconfirmed information.
Notification and release of information follow agency and jurisdiction rules.
Job shadowing and trial observation
Complete records, case file organizing, material circulation and escalation actions under supervision.
Supervisors can review record quality, boundary awareness and escalation judgment item by item.
Assessment and appointment conditions are set by the agency; actions involving bodies, autopsies or signing authority must be carried out within the authorized scope.
Jurisdiction minimum qualifications
Follow state, county or agency official rules (which may involve age, residency, training or examination).
There is no uniform national coroner threshold in the United States.
Able to cite the jurisdiction's current regulatory text to explain the qualification and how the position is filled.
Check against the target state or county rules and do not mix them with other U.S. states or Chinese requirements.
Check the jurisdiction's official position description and regulations first, then consider training.
Qualification rules change with jurisdiction and time, so the effective version must be checked.
How the position is filled (election or appointment)
Some states fill it by election, while others use appointment or run it alongside a medical examiner system.
The election or appointment process determines the term and accountability and is not proof of professional qualification.
Able to explain that state's rules on how this position is filled and its term.
Check against that state's or county's system.
Check how the position is actually filled and its term.
Different states fill it differently, and conclusions from another state cannot be carried over.
Medical or forensic training (medical examiner path)
Applies only to the physician-led forensic pathology direction, which usually requires a medical degree and forensic pathology training.
Must not be written together with coroner qualifications, and cannot be replaced by coroner experience.
Able to explain the education and training stages of this path.
Check against the statutory requirements of the medical examiner system.
Plan the medical path and the coroner path separately.
Training duration and requirements follow medical education and professional body rules.
Death investigation and records training
Courses or supervised training used to build scene response, records and chain of evidence ability.
Courses or certificates usually do not confer a statutory position, autopsy authority or signing authority.
Able to explain how the training content corresponds to actions actually performed.
Check against the provider's and agency's requirements.
Choose training that matches the target position's tasks.
Training is not the same as qualification recognition or work authorization.
Autopsy and medical appraisal authorization
Set by the jurisdiction and usually tied to a pathologist or medical examiner system.

Ordering an autopsy, performing the medical examination, interpreting reports and forming a statutory conclusion each involve position authority and professional ability; check authority item by item and do not lump all reading and interpretation into the same practice act.
Able to cite jurisdictional rules to explain where autopsy authority lies.
Check against the specific jurisdiction and agency.
Confirm which actions the current position can arrange, perform, coordinate or interpret, and refer anything beyond that to the appropriate personnel.
The scope of autopsy authority varies by jurisdiction and must be checked case by case.
Agency authorization and signing responsibility
The law together with the actual position and agency authorization limits who signs statutory documents; agency rules cannot expand statutory powers on their own.
Without the position and authorization, one must not sign statutory documents or act in the name of a coroner.
Able to explain the types of documents signed and the source of that authority.
Check against agency rules and jurisdiction rules.
Clarify which document types you may and may not sign.
Signing responsibility and the authorization chain follow the current system.

Articles 2 and 4—7 of the Ministry of Justice's Provisions on the Classification of Practice for Forensic Judicial Appraisal cover forensic appraisal for specialized litigation issues, forensic pathology, postmortem examination and determination of manner of death; they describe the relevant business, do not establish a position or wage in one-to-one correspondence with the U.S. coroner, and do not provide the complete entry conditions for the target units on this page. values: Visible fictional materials
Fictional report: the discovery location is County B; the intake form is provisionally filled in as County A, and the jurisdiction basis field is blank.
Scene record: discovery time 08:10; the officer's summary states that the scene had been secured at 08:05.
Evidence bag label E-14; the transfer form says E-41.
Rule: only mark contradictions and items to be verified; do not judge jurisdiction, cause of death, manner of death or notify families.
Task
Produce a case file completeness checklist distinguishing facts, contradictions and matters that must be decided by statutory personnel.
Safety boundary
Do not touch bodies or real cases, do not infer cause or manner of death, and do not give conclusions to families or law enforcement.

paragraphs: Output template: ① material facts; ② conflicts or calculations; ③ the exercise rules relied on; ④ provisional conclusion; ⑤ stop conditions; ⑥ reviewer and next steps. Missing information must be written as 'to be verified' and must not be made up.

values: Facts
Transcribe numbers, versions, units or given values item by item
Can be located back in the materials
Judgment
Write the formula or rule and the result
Keep facts and assumptions separate
Boundaries
Write the stop conditions and actions that must not be taken
Do not exceed authority
Handover
Write the items to be verified, the responsible person and the next steps
The successor can review it
Reference answer
The jurisdiction information for County A and County B conflicts and the basis is missing.
The 08:05 securing is earlier than the 08:10 discovery, so the timeline needs to be checked back against the original records.
Evidence numbers E-14 and E-41 are inconsistent; no conclusion is drawn on cause of death, manner of death or jurisdiction.
The reference answer holds only under the rules given in this exercise.
Day 1: read one public material
Find a public material on death investigation or public health death data, mark three requirements about records or authorization, and write down what you want to verify.
Day 2: compile a scene investigation step checklist

Using a fictional scenario, turn the six steps of NIJ 2024 (notification and response, arrival, recording and assessing the scene, recording and assessing the body, recording decedent information, completing the scene investigation) into an actionable checklist.
Day 3: do one record conflict exercise
Using fictional materials, find conflicts in time, place or numbering, compile them into a to-be-verified list, and do not judge cause of death.
Day 4: write one chain of evidence statement
For fictional materials, write a statement of the evidence and transfer chain, marking the recipient, time and status of each transfer, and marking missing information as to be verified.
Day 5: write one escalation and boundary statement
Explain which matters are outside your authority (jurisdiction, cause of death, manner of death, notifying families or signing documents) and to whom you should escalate.
Day 6: have someone else review using only the materials
Have a peer review your conclusions and gap markings using only your materials, and record the questions they raise.
Day 7: review against the standard whether to continue
Return to the judgment checklist on this page and write down three reasons you are willing to continue and two conditions that require caution.

entries: Specific change: can you write clearly, based on fictional materials, the records, conflicts, chain of evidence and escalation conditions, rather than just writing 'pay attention to safety'?
Facts and choices: would you rather do statutory investigations within a jurisdiction, scene and records coordination, or a medical, pathology or public health data direction?
Exercise cost: infection and trauma materials, on-call response, family communication and long record-keeping — which step drains you most, and can it recur in every case?
Material boundary: the exercise materials must all be fictional, and real body images, personal medical information or real case materials must not be used.
Reaction to feedback: when your records are found to have numbering or transfer chain gaps, are you willing to go back to the original materials and fill them in?

Next step: if you are willing to continue with the first five steps, the next step is to complete, under compliant conditions, one closed loop from note verification to jurisdiction qualification verification, and have an experienced person review it.

details: Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((50+25+25)/3+0.5)=33; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.

Anchors: 0 negligible; 25 preparation or record assistance; 50 substantial assistance; 75 most information output can be formed by AI with review; 100 almost all of the selected task can be done by AI and independently verified.

Real inputs include reports and scene observations, body and identity information, medical history, witness statements, photographs, the chain of physical evidence, toxicology or pathology results and law enforcement records. — 50/100; weight=1/3; coroners.profile.work-context-block.2[0]

Editorial process summary: verify jurisdiction and identity, record the scene and body, conduct interviews and take medical history, preserve and transfer physical evidence, examine or arrange autopsy and pathology and toxicology testing, and produce the reports and documents one is authorized to sign. O*NET also lists forensic examination/autopsy and directing autopsies as tasks, so it cannot be summarized as all coroners only organizing paperwork; the executing parties and authorization must be checked separately. — 25/100; weight=1/3; coroners.profile.work-context-block.3[0]

The key judgment is to distinguish observation, testimony and professional inference, and to decide which matters require the involvement of forensic physicians, pathology, toxicology, law enforcement or the courts. — 25/100; weight=1/3; coroners.profile.work-context-block.4[0]

body: Editorial reasoning: in an environment approved by the agency and authorized for data processing, tools may assist with case file field validation, timelines and document drafts; whether they are reliable must be verified. They acquire no statutory authority and do not replace authorized personnel in forming cause/manner of death conclusions or performing autopsy and toxicology analysis. CDC data modernization materials are not evidence of generative AI adoption.

career_risk_cards.direct_answer: Check jurisdiction authority, the chain of evidence and death certification separately, along with scene infection and other safety exposures.

career_risk_cards.heading: Risks and control points for coroners

risks.consequence: The investigation and death certification may lose their legal basis, affecting subsequent judicial and statistical use.
risks.mitigation: First confirm the jurisdiction, competence and where authority lies; if it cannot be confirmed, stop making substantive judgments and escalate.
risks.scenario: Advancing an investigation in the wrong jurisdiction or beyond medical authorization.

risks.consequence: The investigation team and later reviewers may be unable to reconstruct the facts.
risks.mitigation: First record and preserve according to scene safety and applicable authority, leaving a trace of transfers; mark numbering and time conflicts as to be verified, and do not use preserving the original state to exclude safety handling.
risks.scenario: Incomplete scene, identity or chain of evidence records, or inconsistent numbering.

risks.consequence: May mislead families, public records and judicial users.
risks.mitigation: Clearly mark provisional status and the basis; the final conclusion is formed by those with authority according to procedures.
risks.scenario: Writing preliminary observations as a final cause or manner of death.

risks.consequence: Registration agencies and public health statistics may receive erroneous data.
risks.mitigation: Check fields against the individual case materials and jurisdiction rules, and refer doubts to the jurisdiction's responsible person for confirmation.
risks.scenario: Death certificate fields missing or an inapplicable template applied.

risks.affected_roles: Responding investigators, body examination personnel and collaborating teams
risks.consequence: Investigators may be injured or exposed; inadequate safety also hinders the investigation.
risks.mitigation: Editorial suggestion: handle entry, protection and exposure reporting according to the agency's assessment, training and authorization; this page did not obtain a suspension and recovery procedure for specific scenarios.
risks.scenario: Facing infection and environmental risks when arriving on scene or contacting bodies or scene materials.

risks.mitigation: Stop and escalate along the authorization chain.
risks.scenario: Encountering tasks beyond the authorized scope.

description.text: Coroners carry statutory coordination of death investigations, but how the position is created, whether it must be held by a physician, and whether it can order an autopsy or issue documents all vary by jurisdiction; the core is to turn the scene, the body, identity, medical history and examination materials into a traceable conclusion.
